rule: This register is the stratum's own answer to docs/NON_CLAIMS.md: it records, per surface, whether it is `claimed` (a passing court covers it) or `bounded` (explicitly outside this stratum -- including no FIPS validation, no universal parity from finite evidence, and memory safety measured rather than established). It is authored, not derived: the `CUSTODIAN-BOUNDARY-REGISTER` court in forensics/tools/phase20_courts.py re-reads the four passing custodian courts' own records (the claimed side) and the constitution/limitations artefacts docs/NON_CLAIMS.md, docs/FIPS_CLAIMS.md, docs/UNSAFE.md and the unsafe-footprint growth ceiling (the bounded side), and fails the stratum if any recorded boundary has drifted from the evidence that establishes it (docs/PHASE-20-SUBPHASES.md section 3.6). A surface no passing court reaches is `bounded`, never `claimed`, and the register may claim no more than the courts above measured.

surfaces.surface: the L0-L9 maturity ladder derivation for libcrypto and libssl, and the gap to the L9 high-assurance custodian seal the seal names
surfaces.note: claimed, not a property claim: the passing court derived the ladder from committed evidence, so the *derivation* is covered -- but the L9 level the seal names is the level this stratum is still establishing, and the court records the gap as the finding below, so the property reads NOT_CLAIMED. A passing RT-CUSTODIAN-MATURITY must never be read as 'L9 custodian seal achieved' (docs/PHASE-20-SUBPHASES.md section 4.2).

surfaces.surface: the join of every in-scope obligation to its FRF receipt, with the covering sensitivity-backed claim carrying zero blockers
surfaces.note: claimed as an instrument: the passing court executed the join over the finite receipts the store carries. It is not a universal-parity claim -- the join is over the receipts the FRF store records, and the three non-claims below still bound it (docs/CUSTODIAN_CONTRACT.md section 6).

surfaces.surface: the disposition of every residual, with no UNKNOWN residual intersecting the claimed production profile
surfaces.note: claimed, not a residual closure beyond the profile: the passing court dispositioned every residual it read and found zero UNKNOWN residuals intersecting a declared compatibility root. An UNKNOWN residual that merely does not intersect is recorded, not resolved -- UNKNOWN remains a result, not a resting state (docs/CUSTODIAN_CONTRACT.md sections 6 and 8, docs/PARITY_MODEL.md section 1).

surfaces.surface: the ABI-substitution witness chain and the machine-owned downstream corpus witness chain, re-established current and functional
surfaces.note: claimed, bounded to the witnesses read: the passing court re-derived the nine witnesses (three ABI-substitution, six downstream) as current and functional from the machine-owned records. It does not re-run the Phase-17 harnesses -- it proves currency by candidate identity -- so it witnesses those binaries over that corpus, not downstream completeness (docs/PHASE-20-SUBPHASES.md section 3.5).

surfaces.surface: FIPS formal validation of the candidate
surfaces.note: bounded: docs/FIPS_CLAIMS.md section 1 separates FIPS behavioural parity (implemented and courted) from FIPS formal validation (an external certification process), and section 3 labels the candidate NOT FIPS VALIDATED. Behavioural parity with the FIPS provider is not validation, and OpenSSL's own certification is never used to imply certification of openssl-rs (docs/NON_CLAIMS.md section 3).

surfaces.surface: a universal-parity or drop-in-replacement claim from finite evidence
surfaces.note: bounded: docs/NON_CLAIMS.md section 1 forbids '100% OpenSSL compatible' or 'drop-in OpenSSL replacement' without the supported authority / version / build profile / platform scope immediately adjacent, and section 2 derives any headline from evidence-bearing obligations rather than typing it. Every claim in this stratum names its authority, profile, platform, court and evidence (docs/CUSTODIAN_CONTRACT.md section 7).

surfaces.surface: established memory safety, as distinct from a measured unsafe footprint
surfaces.note: bounded: docs/UNSAFE.md section 2 says unsafe is measured, not asserted, and that the measurement is not a memory-safety claim -- a footprint is not a proof, and the crate has had memory-safety defects of exactly the class Rust is meant to remove. forensics/atlas/unsafe-footprint.json records the measured footprint and artifacts/phase18/unsafe-bounds.json records the core-module growth ceiling the HOSTILE-BOUNDARY-REGISTER court enforces; a ceiling is a ratchet, not a proof that any unsafe block is correct (docs/NON_CLAIMS.md section 3).

surfaces.surface: the L9 high-assurance custodian seal itself
surfaces.note: bounded: L9 high-assurance custodian seal is the level Phase 20 itself is establishing, and its evidence docs/PHASE-20-CUSTODIAN-SEAL.md is absent until 20.6 lands it (docs/PHASE-20-SUBPHASES.md section 4.2). The maturity court records the gap to L9 as a finding, so the register does not claim the level; a passing custodian court is an instrument, not the property it names.
